notes:
These verses are a list of town names. The commentaries mostly explain where the towns were, link them to other Bible stories, and try to make sense of the town counts in v. 32 and v. 36. I didn't find any notes for v. 40.

**Overview (vv. 21–42 as a section)**
- **Structure:** Barnes says the towns are arranged in four regions by landscape: the Negeb or south country Joshua 15:21-32; of "the valley," or "the plain" ("Shephelah", Joshua 15:33-47); of "the mountains" Joshua 15:48-60; and of "the wilderness". He adds that many of the identifications are still conjectural only. https://www.studylight.org/bible/eng/asv/joshua/15-33.html ; https://biblehub.com/commentaries/joshua/15-21.htm
- **Why a list of names matters:** Guzik says the list shows these were real places, not the description of a symbolic or spiritual inheritance. He quotes Madvig, who calls such lists evidence of the historical, down-to-earth nature of God's redemptive program. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/joshua-15-16-17/
- **Where the list comes from in Scripture:** Precept Austin quotes Dale Ralph Davis, who calls Joshua 15 "promise geography," one of the buds on the tree of Genesis 12 and Genesis 15. Davis also warns against reading it without spicing it up with any spirtualising additives. https://www.preceptaustin.org/joshua-15-commentary
- **What isn't listed:** Matthew Henry notes that Bethlehem doesn't appear. He suggests it was now so little as not to be accounted one of the cities, but perhaps was one of the villages not named. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/joshua/15-32.html

**v. 22:** The Cambridge Bible suggests Kinah was possibly the territory of the Kenites who settled at Arad. It equates Dimonah with Dibon (Neh. 11:25). Of the first 29 southern towns, Ellicott says Conder identified only four, Adadah among them. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/joshua/15-21.htm

**v. 23:** The Cambridge Bible says Kedesh, Hazor and Ithnan are unknown. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/joshua/15-21.htm

**v. 24:** Barnes says Telem may be the Telaim of 1 Samuel 15:4, where Saul mustered his army for the expedition against the Amalekites. https://www.studylight.org/bible/jpn/kyb/joshua/15-39.html

**v. 25:**
- Barnes explains the names: Kerioth, prefixed to a name, bespeaks military occupation, as Hazor points to pastoral pursuits. He thinks the Anakim fortified an old herders' settlement, and Judah later added the name Hezron after one of its ancestors. https://www.studylight.org/bible/jpn/kyb/joshua/15-39.html
- Ellicott notes that some see a trace of Kerioth in the sobriquet of Judas Is-cariot, the man of Kerioth. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/joshua/15-21.htm
- Barnes thinks the King James Version may have split names that were one in the Hebrew. He gives v. 25 as an example. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/joshua/15-62.html

**vv. 26–28:**
- Constable groups the third nine (Joshua 15:26-28). https://www.studylight.org/commentary/joshua/15-32.html
- **Beersheba (v. 28):** The Pulpit Commentary names Beersheba and Hormah as the only places of any importance in Scripture history in this southern list. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/joshua/15-21.htm
- BibleHub's verse study notes that "from Dan to Beersheba" became shorthand for the whole land. It also connects Beersheba with Abraham's oath and Isaac's wells. https://biblehub.com/joshua/15-28.htm
- **Biziothiah (v. 28):** BibleHub's study says the name may mean "contempt of the Lord," though the significance of this name is not clear from the biblical text. https://biblehub.com/joshua/15-28.htm

**vv. 29–30:**
- **Chesil (v. 30):** Barnes says the name Chesil, meaning "fool," was most likely bestowed by way of opprobrium, much as Bethel ("house of God") was mocked as Bethaven. Since the word also means Orion, he thinks star worship may have gone on there. https://www.studylight.org/bible/pol/was/joshua/15-39.html
- **Hormah (v. 30):** The Pulpit Commentary says Judges 1:17 explains why Hormah is listed among Simeon's towns as well as Judah's. It calls this another instance of the remarkable accuracy of our author. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/joshua/15-21.htm

**v. 31 (Ziklag):** Ellicott points out that Ziklag came to Judah's kings through a gift from Achish to David, not through Joshua. He says this shows the partial character of the conquest and the division of unconquered territory to the tribes. The Pulpit Commentary adds that the Amalekites later burned it (1 Sam. 30:1). https://biblehub.com/commentaries/joshua/15-21.htm

**v. 32:**
- **Ain and Rimmon:** The Pulpit Commentary thinks these are more likely the name of one place Ain-Rimmon, the fountain of the god Rimmon. Keil and Delitzsch say the two were probably so close together that in the course of time they grew into one. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/joshua/15-32.htm
- **Why "twenty-nine" when more names are listed:** The older commentators disagree here. This is a matter of interpretation, not a split between churches.
  - Clarke (Wesleyan/Methodist) gives the traditional view: nine of the 38 towns were afterwards given to the tribe of Simeon. He then suggests a likelier answer: translators may have turned descriptive words into separate cities. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/joshua/15-32.html
  - Gill (Baptist) reports that Jewish commentators Rashi (Jarchi) and Kimchi gave the Simeon explanation. He finds it unsatisfying and prefers Abarbanel's view: the 29 were proper cities, and the other were villages, unwalled towns, or not of so much note. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/joshua/15-32.html
  - Matthew Henry agrees with the Simeon explanation. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/joshua/15-54.html
  - Poole offers both answers: the extra towns went to Simeon, or only walled cities were counted. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/joshua/15-32.htm
  - The Pulpit Commentary calls it a copying error: The actual number is thirty-six. The error is as old as the LXX. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/joshua/15-32.htm
  - Keil and Delitzsch blame a copyist mixing up similar number-letters. They reject the theory that later names were added without fixing the total, saying it presupposes greater thoughtlessness on the part of the editor than we have any right to attribute to the author. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/joshua/15-32.htm
  - Guzik passes on Clarke's Simeon explanation. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/joshua-15-16-17/

**v. 33:**
- **The foothills:** Barnes describes the Shephelah as of an undulating surface and highly fertile character. Its towns, like the southern ones, fall into four groups. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/joshua/15-33.htm
- Precept Austin says these hills rise 500 to 700 feet and provided a natural barrier to the Hebrew peoples living inland. https://www.preceptaustin.org/joshua-15-commentary
- **Eshtaol and Zorah:** Clarke says Samson was buried here and that the towns later went to Dan (Josh. 19:41). https://www.studylight.org/commentary/joshua/15-33.html
- Precept Austin adds that Samson's family was among the Danites pushed into these hills. It quotes Holman's dictionary: Eshtaol means "asking (for an oracle)" and Zorah means "wasps" or "hornets." https://www.preceptaustin.org/joshua-15-commentary

**vv. 34–35:** Matthew Henry lists Adullam among the places where David hid from Saul. He says David kept as close to it as he could to the Lord's inheritance. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/joshua/15-32.html

**v. 36:**
- Henry says the text counts fourteen but names fifteen. He thinks Gederah and Gederothaim were probably either two names or two parts of one and the same city. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/joshua/15-33.html
- Keil and Delitzsch list this verse as another case of the total not matching the names. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/joshua/15-32.htm

**vv. 37–38:**
- Constable says this group has 16 in the northwest (Joshua 15:37-41). https://www.studylight.org/commentary/joshua/15-33.html
- **Joktheel (v. 38):** Holman's dictionary (via Precept Austin) says the name means "God nourishes" or "destroys." It notes that Amaziah later gave the same name to Selah in Edom. https://www.preceptaustin.org/joshua-15-commentary

**v. 39:**
- Gill notes that Lachish and Eglon were royal cities (Josh. 10:3). King Josiah's mother came from Bozkath. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/joshua/15-39.htm
- Lange says Rehoboam fortified Lachish and King Amaziah died there. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/lcc/joshua-15.html
- Matthew Henry, citing Micah 1:13, says Lachish was the beginning of sin to the daughter of Zion. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/joshua/15-37.html
- BibleHub's study draws an application from Bozkath: God often uses quiet corners of His kingdom for significant impact. https://biblehub.com/joshua/15-39.htm

**v. 41:** Here the group closes: "sixteen cities." Constable's total for vv. 37–41 is given under vv. 37–38. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/joshua/15-33.html

**v. 42:**
- Constable starts a new group of nine in the south (Joshua 15:42-44). https://www.studylight.org/commentary/joshua/15-33.html
- Guzik's notes on Joshua 19 say the Shephelah towns of v. 42 include towns that went to Simeon. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/joshua-18-19/
- Henry notes that Libnah later revolted in the days of King Joram (2 Kings 8:22). https://www.studylight.org/commentary/joshua/15-37.html

**What I couldn't find**
- **Differences between Protestant traditions:** None. The Baptist (Gill), Methodist (Clarke) and other older writers only differ on how to count the towns in vv. 32 and 36.
- **Other views:** I found no modern scholarship (Bible Odyssey, NET notes), no Catholic or Orthodox readings, and no prosperity or word-of-faith teaching on these verses. BibleHub's study pages do apply Judah's land to believers' "spiritual inheritance in Christ." That is a general devotional application, not one of those movements.
- **Gaps in my reading:** I ran out of searches, so I couldn't read the Haydock (Catholic) commentary on BibleHub or Precept Austin's verse notes for vv. 22–42. Those are worth checking next.
